Chapter 9: Decluttering Through Life Transitions
Major life changes—like moving, downsizing, welcoming a new family member, or handling a loss—tend to bring both a fresh wave of clutter and a swirl of emotions.
But you know what? These moments are actually powerful opportunities. They give you a chance to pause, reassess what truly matters, and let go of what no longer fits your life right now.
If you’re about to move, think of packing as more than just putting things in boxes. What if you looked at each item and asked yourself, “Does this really deserve a spot in my new home? Or is it time to let it go?” It’s a simple question, but it can make all the difference. And if you’re downsizing, focus on the essentials—the things that actually bring you joy or serve a real purpose. Everything else? Maybe it’s time to pass it along to someone who’ll appreciate it.
Welcoming a new child or blending two households? That usually means a sudden flood of toys, clothes, and all sorts of shared stuff. Here’s where the Container Concept comes in handy—set clear limits for what you keep. Maybe each child gets one bin for toys, or you agree on one closet for shared things. It helps keep everything manageable and gives everyone a sense of order.
And when you’re coping with loss, remember to be gentle with yourself. There’s absolutely no rush to sort through a loved one’s things. Take it one step at a time, and don’t hesitate to reach out for support if you need it. Sometimes, just talking things through with someone else can lighten the load.
So, here are a few gentle reminders to help you navigate these transitions:
Give yourself permission to let go of things that no longer serve you. Focus on creating a home that supports your life as it is now—your needs, your values. Involve your family in the decisions, but remember, everyone moves at their own pace and feels things differently. That’s okay.
Sure, transitions can be stressful. But they’re also a chance for renewal—a fresh start. With a bit of intention and self-compassion, you really can create a living space that reflects who you are today, not just who you used to be.
